draft.title: Types of business
card: Sole trader
one person owns and runs the business. They keep all profit and make all decisions.
Partnership
two or more people own the business together and share the profit. They usually agree how to split the work and the decisions.
Company

a company is a separate legal entity owned by shareholders. A private limited company has a few shareholders and its shares are not sold on the share market. A public listed company sells shares on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX).
Other types
A social enterprise aims mainly to help a community or cause, and uses its profit for that aim. A government business enterprise is owned by government and sells goods or services to earn revenue.
draft.remember: The type of business is chosen to suit who owns it and what the owners want from it.

a.q: Which type of business is owned by shareholders and sells its shares on the share market?
a.why: A public listed company sells its shares on the ASX, so anyone can buy them. A private limited company also has shareholders, but its shares are not sold on the share market.
a.clue: Think about which business has shares that anyone can buy.

b.q: Priya starts a bakery in Ballarat. She wants to hire and train people who have been out of work, and spend any profit on this work. Which type of business best fits her aim?
b.why: A social enterprise aims mainly to help a community or cause, and uses its profit for that aim. A sole trader keeps the profit for the owner, so it does not fit Priya's aim of spending profit on helping others.
b.clue: Look at what Priya wants to do with the profit.

problems.detail: The why says a sole trader 'keeps the profit for the owner, so it does not fit Priya's aim'. A social enterprise describes a business's purpose, not a legal structure, so a social enterprise can be run as a sole trader. A sole trader can also spend profit on a cause. The why should only say a social enterprise fits her aim best, not that a sole trader cannot.

'A private limited company has a few shareholders' is vague. A proprietary limited company in Australia can have up to 50 non-employee shareholders, so 'a limited number of shareholders' would be more accurate.

check.summary: Both questions have a clear, correct answer. The why for (b) wrongly treats a sole trader and a social enterprise as mutually exclusive, and the card's 'a few shareholders' for private companies is vague.
